expected_effect: Full 1800 s run on the same host: steps +3% to +12% vs control (2071/2076), public_val_bpb lower by 0.001 to 0.005 (predicted ~1.001-1.004 vs 1.0057/1.0060). Smoke (300 s): steps >= 1.02x same-host control smoke (>=342 vs 334/335) with smoke BPB <= control smoke. Falsified if steps are within +/-1% of control (head matmul not a cost) or if steps rise >= 2% but BPB does not improve (BF16 logit rounding harms quality).
hypothesis: Under the pinned control environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', no '--auto-cast matmult --auto-cast-type bf16'), any F.linear/matmul in train.py whose operands are not explicitly cast runs in FP32 on Trainium. The KEEP result for --bf16-sdpa-input (2233 steps / 1.002028 vs 2076 / 1.005967 same-host control: +7.6% steps, -0.0039 BPB) shows that (a) such un-cast FP32 boundaries exist in the pinned default graph and (b) casting one of them to BF16 converts step-rate into fixed-budget BPB gain with no measurable quality loss. The final LM-head logits projection (final hidden states x head weight, vocab-sized output, executed every micro-step in forward and backward) is the largest remaining dense matmul that is not covered by any tested flag at this commit; every fresh-start ledger run that reached <0.99 BPB ran this projection in BF16 via compiler autocast, which the controller forbids as an env change. Casting only the head matmul operands to BF16 and up-casting the logits back to FP32 before softcap/cross-entropy will raise steps in 1800 s by 3-12% (proportional to the head's share of FLOPs) and lower public_val_bpb by 0.001-0.005 versus the same-host control.
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-bf16-lm-head-logits-matmul-only from 9a4caa7b. Step 0 (static check, before editing): locate the model's final logits projection -- the F.linear / matmul / (tied) wte-weight product that maps the final-normed hidden state [B,T,d] to vocab-sized logits, immediately upstream of the softcap and cross-entropy (the region gated by the --nki-softcap-ce and --byte-loss-weight options). Read the code path under default flags (bf16_norm_output False, bf16_sdpa_input False) and record the dtype of each operand. If both operands are already torch.bfloat16 at that call, or the call sits inside a torch.autocast context, stop and return HALT-INERT. Step 1: following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add a module-level constant USE_BF16_LM_HEAD = True with the same style of environment override (NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_LM_HEAD, '0' disables) and a matching argparse pair --bf16-lm-head / --no-bf16-lm-head (dest bf16_lm_head, default None -> falls back to the constant); default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. Step 2: at the logits projection only, when USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is True, replace the call with: h16 = h.to(torch.bfloat16); w16 = head_weight.to(torch.bfloat16) (head_weight is whatever tensor the current code uses -- lm_head.weight or the tied wte.weight; do not change tying, do not create a new Parameter, do not change initialization); logits = F.linear(h16, w16) (or the equivalent matmul form already used, preserving any transposed-linear layout the code selects); logits = logits.float(). Leave every downstream operation (softcap, cross-entropy, byte-loss weighting, eval BPB accumulation, causality check) byte-for-byte unchanged so they receive FP32 logits as before. Autograd propagates gradients through the .to() casts to the FP32 master weight; no optimizer or grad-clip code changes. The same forward code path must serve training and evaluation; do not add a separate eval branch. When USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is False the original call must execute unchanged. Step 3: add exactly one field 'bf16_lm_head=<bool>' to the existing config oneliner that already prints bf16_sdpa_input/bf16_norm_output-style precision options so the resolved value appears in the ledger. Step 4: no other edits: no changes to attention, norms, MLP, ngram-ve tables, kernels, schedule, batch, seed handling, evaluator, or NEURON_CC_FLAGS handling. Verification for the implementation verifier: (a) diff limited to the constant/env/CLI toggle, the head-boundary cast block, and the one log field; (b) grep confirms softcap/CE code untouched; (c) with the env override set to '0' the code path is the original; (d) smoke run resolves bf16_lm_head=True, num_params_M 592.9, ngram_ve oneliner identical to control, and meets the smoke gate above.
single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change in train.py: at the LM-head logits projection only, cast the final hidden-state activation and the head weight (a temporary .to(torch.bfloat16) view; the FP32 master parameter, its optimizer state, and any tied wte lookup are untouched) so the logits matmul executes in BF16, then immediately .float() the logits so softcap, cross-entropy, byte-loss weighting, evaluation BPB, and the causality check consume FP32 logits exactly as before. Everything else stays at 9a4caa7b defaults: no --bf16-sdpa-input, no --bf16-norm-output, no --nki-* or --compile-* flag, no optimizer/schedule/batch/architecture/ngram-ve change, identical launch shape and environment as the pinned controls, num_params_M must remain 592.9. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967). Outcome classes evaluated in order: (1) HALT-INERT if the static pre-implementation check finds the head matmul already executes with both operands BF16 (or under an autocast context) in the default configuration -- do not implement or launch; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control (head matmul is not a measurable cost); (4) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% of control (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): record throughput and BPB, and before any quality claim compare the candidate's logged validation trajectory with the control's at matched step counts; if matched-step trajectories are unavailable, quality attribution is recorded as unresolved; SUCCESS may still be declared only if public_val_bpb < control by >= 0.001 and no matched-step deficit > 0.010 at the control's final step; (5) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control (BF16 logit rounding costs more than the recovered steps); (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
